title: Connect Your Team
subtitle: Join your team's shared workspace and connect the desktop AI app you already use. Everyone keeps their own app — memory, runs, and approvals stay in sync across the whole team.
loginRequired: Please sign in to connect with your team.

teams.title: Your teams
teams.joinDesc: Got an invite code from a teammate? Paste it here to join their team.
teams.noTeams: You're not on any team yet
teams.noTeamsDesc: Join with an invite code above, or ask a teammate to invite you.

guide.title: Connect your desktop app
guide.desc: Every teammate connects their own app to the same team server. Pick your app below, paste the snippet, and sign in once — you're working with the team.
guide.endpointHint: Same URL for every app and every teammate — sign-in is discovered automatically (OAuth 2.1).

claude.name: Claude Desktop
claude.step1: Open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
claude.step2: Name it “AI Swarm Studio” and paste your team MCP server URL — or merge the snippet below into claude_desktop_config.json.
claude.step3: Click Connect — a browser window opens for sign-in.
claude.step4: Approve access. Team tools now appear in every conversation.

chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt.step1: Go to Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings and enable Developer Mode.
chatgpt.step2: Create a new app and paste the URL below as the connector endpoint.
chatgpt.step3: ChatGPT discovers the OAuth flow automatically — sign in when prompted.
chatgpt.step4: Mention the app in any chat to see team runs waiting for you.

qwen.name: Qwen Code
qwen.step1: Add the team server from your terminal:
qwen.step2: Qwen Code stores the server in ~/.qwen/settings.json.
qwen.step3: On first use a browser opens for OAuth sign-in — approve access.
qwen.step4: Ask Qwen Code about team runs; it calls the tools directly.

kimi.name: Kimi
kimi.step1: Open Settings → MCP Servers → Add Server.
kimi.step2: Choose the streamable HTTP transport and paste the URL below.
kimi.step3: Save, then click Authorize to complete OAuth sign-in.
kimi.step4: Team tools appear in new conversations.

handoff.title: “Waiting for you” — approvals that cross apps
handoff.desc: When a teammate's run pauses for approval, they can hand the decision off to you. It shows up inside YOUR desktop app — approve it there and the run resumes in theirs. Nobody switches apps.
handoff.step1Desc: A teammate's pipeline hits an approval step while they're away or busy.
handoff.step2Desc: They assign the approval to you. It appears as “waiting for you” in whichever app you use.
handoff.step3Desc: Approve or reject from your own app. The run resumes instantly for your teammate.
handoff.noteDesc: Once you're connected, handoffs arrive automatically in your app's tool list — nothing else to install or configure.
